name: Zahara
description: Manage Zahara invoices, purchase orders, suppliers, projects, users, and tenancy data.

authentication.name: Zahara API Keys
authentication.description: Use the tenancy API key, business unit API key, and tenancy ID from Zahara.

credentials.name: Tenancy API Key
credentials.description: API key from Zahara Admin > Settings > Integrations for tenancy-level endpoints.

credentials.name: Business Unit API Key
credentials.description: Business unit API key returned from the Zahara BusinessUnit endpoint for business-unit endpoints.

credentials.name: Tenancy ID
credentials.description: Tenancy identifier used for Zahara reporting and premium data workflows.

setupGuide.title: Get your Zahara API credentials
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zahara login with an active tenant or trial and access to the Zahara admin settings for that tenant.

steps.title: Create or confirm your Zahara tenant access
steps.description: Sign in to an active Zahara tenant. If you do not have access yet, start a trial or ask your Zahara admin to invite you.

steps.title: Copy the tenancy API key
steps.description: In Zahara, open the admin settings and go to the Integrations area. Copy the tenancy API key for your tenant.

steps.title: Get the business unit API key
steps.description: Use Zahara's Get Business Units endpoint with your tenancy API key. Zahara's documentation says this endpoint returns every business setting for the tenancy. From the business unit you want to use, copy the business unit API key from the returned settings.

steps.title: Get the tenancy ID if you will use reporting
steps.description: If you will use reporting or SmartSync+ exports, copy the tenancy ID for the same tenant. Zahara's reporting guide says the tenancy ID is usually hidden and may need to be provided by Zahara.

name: Zaia
description: Manage AI agents, squads, workflows, channels, and support

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use a Zaia Endless workspace API key.
authentication.notes: Zaia documents a required authorization header whose value is the raw workspace API key. The workspace ID is useful connection metadata but is not required for GET /api/v1/agents authentication.

setupGuide.title: Connect Zaia
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Zaia Endless workspace you want to connect.

steps.title: Open your workspace settings
steps.description: In Zaia Endless, open the workspace you want MindCloud to use, then go to the workspace settings area.

steps.title: Copy the workspace API key
steps.description: Open the API keys section in workspace settings and copy an active API key for the workspace.

steps.title: Copy the workspace ID
steps.description: In the Overview section of workspace settings, copy the Workspace ID if you want it saved with the connection for reference.

setupGuide.title: Connect Zakeke
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zakeke merchant account and access to its back office.

steps.title: Sign in to the Zakeke admin area
steps.description: Open the Zakeke admin login page and sign in with the merchant account you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Copy your API credentials
steps.description: Open Your Account > API keys and copy the Client ID and Client Secret for the account.

steps.title: Confirm the sales channel integration settings
steps.description: Open Sales Channels > Integration settings and API Keys, then verify the Store URL, Products Catalog API URL, and Base Currency are filled in for the connected store.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Back in MindCloud, enter the Zakeke Client ID and Client Secret, then run Authenticate. MindCloud will request an S2S access token using the client credentials flow.

name: Zendesk
description: Manage tickets, answer customers, build help centers, and track service.

authentication.name: API token
authentication.description: Basic authentication using a Zendesk email address and API token.

credentials.name: Subdomain
credentials.description: Zendesk account subdomain (for example, mindcloudhelp).

setupGuide.title: Connect Zendesk with an API token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zendesk administrator account to create the API token, plus the Subdomain, Email address, and API token values for the connection form. Zendesk shows the full API token only once when you create it.

steps.title: Turn on API token access in Zendesk
steps.description: In Zendesk Admin Center, go to Apps and integrations > APIs > API configuration. If this is your first time using the API, accept the terms and click Get started. Turn on Allow API token access and click Save.

steps.title: Create an API token

setupGuide.title: Connect Zenlogin
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to your Zenlogin account's API Credentials page.

steps.title: Open your Zenlogin API Credentials page
steps.description: In Zenlogin, go to the API Credentials page for the application you want to connect.

steps.title: Copy the secret key
steps.description: Copy the account secret key. MindCloud sends it as the X_API_SECRET_KEY header on Zenlogin requests.

steps.title: Copy the application key
steps.description: Copy the application key from the endpoint path. It is the value after /applications/ and before /logins/checks.

arguments.name: User Agent
arguments.description: User agent observed during the login attempt. Maximum length is 512 characters.

arguments.name: IP Address

arguments.name: Identity First Name
arguments.description: Optional first name for notification template variables. Maximum length is 256 characters.

arguments.description: Optional last name for notification template variables. Maximum length is 256 characters.

arguments.description: Optional full name for notification template variables. Maximum length is 256 characters.

arguments.name: Process Request
arguments.description: Optional 0 or 1 flag controlling whether Zenlogin should process this login check.

authentication.name: OAuth2
authentication.description: Connect a Zeplin account with OAuth 2.0

setupGuide.title: Connect Zeplin
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zeplin account and a Zeplin app with OAuth client credentials.

steps.title: Open the Developer tab in Zeplin
steps.description: In the Zeplin web app, open your profile page and select Developer.

steps.title: Create or open your Zeplin app
steps.description: Create an app if needed, then copy its Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Add MindCloud's redirect URI to your Zeplin app
steps.description: When you start the MindCloud OAuth connection, use the exact redirect URI MindCloud shows and add it to your Zeplin app configuration.

steps.title: Authenticate the connection in MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud, start the Zeplin connection, and complete the Zeplin authorization screen.

name: Zillow Agent Reviews
description: Bridge-hosted Zillow Agent Reviews data access. Requires a Bridge account and access to the reviews dataset.

authentication.name: Bridge server token
authentication.description: Bridge server token used as the access_token value for Bridge-hosted Zillow Agent Reviews requests.
authentication.notes: Use the Bridge server token from your Bridge dashboard as the apiKey credential; MindCloud injects it into the `access_token` query parameter. Agent Reviews access requires Zillow approval for the application on Bridge before runtime requests will succeed.

setupGuide.title: Connect your Bridge account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Bridge account with Zillow Agent Reviews access approved before this app can return live data.

steps.title: Sign in to Bridge
steps.description: Open the Bridge dashboard for the application that will be connected to MindCloud.

steps.title: Confirm Agent Reviews approval
steps.description: Check Bridge Data Access and confirm the Zillow Agent Reviews product is approved for this application.

steps.title: Copy the Bridge server token
steps.description: Open your API tokens in Bridge and copy the Server token for this application.

name: Zoho Analytics
description: Manage Zoho Analytics workspaces, views, tables, and data

credentials.name: Analytics Server URL
credentials.description: Zoho Analytics API server URL for your data center. Use the exact server URI from Zoho's Server URI table, such as https://analyticsapi.zoho.com or https://analyticsapi.zoho.eu.

credentials.name: Organization ID
credentials.description: Optional default Zoho Analytics organization ID. Run Get Organizations after connecting to find it, then save the organization you use most often.

setupGuide.title: Connect Zoho Analytics
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zoho Analytics account and a Zoho OAuth server-based application. If you already have a Client ID and Client Secret, you can skip the client-creation step.

steps.title: Confirm your Zoho Analytics data center
steps.description: Open the Zoho Analytics API Specification page and find the Server URI table. Choose the Analytics server URL that matches your Zoho data center, such as https://analyticsapi.zoho.com, https://analyticsapi.zoho.eu, https://analyticsapi.zoho.in, https://analyticsapi.zoho.com.au, https://analyticsapi.zoho.com.cn, https://analyticsapi.zoho.jp, https://analyticsapi.zoho.sa, or https://analyticsapi.zohocloud.ca. You will enter this exact value in the Analytics Server URL field in MindCloud.

steps.title: Create or review a Zoho server-based OAuth client
steps.description: In Zoho API Console, create a server-based application for Zoho Analytics, or open the existing one you want to use with MindCloud.

steps.title: Add the MindCloud redirect URL
steps.description: In the Zoho OAuth client settings, add the exact redirect URL shown in MindCloud to the allowed redirect URIs for this app. The redirect URL in Zoho must match MindCloud exactly.

steps.title: Paste your credentials and Analytics server URL into MindCloud
steps.description: Enter the Client ID and Client Secret from Zoho into this connection. In the Analytics Server URL field, paste the exact Analytics API server URL for your data center from step 1.

steps.title: Connect, then save your default organization ID
steps.description: Click Connect and complete the Zoho consent screen. After the connection succeeds, run Get Organizations, copy the organization ID you use most often, and save it in the optional Organization ID field for this connection.

setupGuide.title: Connect Zoho Billing
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zoho Billing account and a Zoho API Console server-based application.

steps.title: Open your Zoho API Console application
steps.description: Go to the Zoho API Console, then open the server-based app you want to use for Zoho Billing. If you do not have one yet, create a server-based application first.

steps.title: Add the MindCloud redirect URL
steps.description: In your Zoho app settings, add the Redirect URL shown in MindCloud to the allowed redirect URIs for this OAuth app.

steps.title: Enable the right data centers if needed
steps.description: If the Zoho Billing users who will connect are outside your app's home data center, enable those data centers in the Zoho API Console. If you want one client secret to work across enabled data centers, choose the option to use the same OAuth credentials for all data centers.

steps.title: Paste your client credentials into this connection
steps.description: Enter the Client ID and Client Secret from Zoho into the MindCloud connection form, then click Connect.

steps.title: Authorize and capture your default organization
steps.description: Complete the Zoho consent screen. After the connection succeeds, run List Organizations, copy the organization_id for the org you use most often, and save it in the optional Organization ID field for this connection.

credentials.description: Zoho Books data center suffix from your app URL. Use com, eu, in, com.au, jp, ca, com.cn, or sa.

setupGuide.title: Set up Zoho Books OAuth
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zoho account with access to Zoho Books. If you already have a Client ID and Client Secret, you can skip the client-creation step.

steps.title: Open Zoho Developer Console
steps.description: Sign in with the Zoho account that manages your Zoho Books organization.

steps.title: Create or review a server-based client
steps.description: Choose Server-based Applications. Enter a client name, your homepage URL, and the exact redirect URI that MindCloud shows during connection setup, then click CREATE.

steps.title: Copy the client credentials into MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the Client ID and Client Secret into this app configuration so MindCloud can start the Zoho OAuth flow.

steps.title: Confirm your Zoho domain
steps.description: Open your Zoho Books web app and note the domain suffix in the URL, such as com, eu, in, com.au, jp, ca, com.cn, or sa. Enter that value in the Zoho Domain field.

steps.title: Enable Multi DC if this client will be used outside its original data center
steps.description: In Zoho Developer Console, enable Multi DC for the client when Zoho documents that your users may authenticate from different Zoho regions.

setupGuide.title: Connect Zoho Cliq
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to a Zoho API Console Server-based application for Zoho Cliq.

steps.title: Open Zoho API Console
steps.description: Open Zoho API Console and create a Server-based Application for Zoho Cliq, or open the existing OAuth client you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Register the exact MindCloud redirect URI
steps.description: Add this redirect URI exactly in your Zoho client settings: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/zohoCliq/callback . Zoho requires an exact redirect URI match.

steps.title: Copy the client credentials into MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the Zoho Client ID and Client Secret into the Zoho Cliq connection form in MindCloud.

steps.title: Authenticate and approve the requested scopes
steps.description: Continue the OAuth popup in MindCloud and approve the Zoho Cliq scopes needed for channel, chat, message, reminder, and profile-read actions. If your Zoho tenant uses a non-.com data center, use the matching Zoho Accounts host before authenticating.

name: Zoho Connect
description: Zoho Connect is Zoho's workplace social network and collaboration platform for networks, groups, feeds, tasks, events, and people discovery.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Connect Zoho Connect with a Zoho OAuth 2.0 client and authorize the required Zoho Connect scopes.
authentication.scopes: zohopulse.networklist.READ zohopulse.userDetail.READ zohopulse.feedList.READ zohopulse.feedList.CREATE zohopulse.tasks.READ zohopulse.tasks.CREATE zohopulse.tasks.UPDATE zohopulse.events.CREATE zohopulse.events.UPDATE zohopulse.events.DELETE zohopulse.grouplist.CREATE zohopulse.grouplist.DELETE

credentials.name: Network ID
credentials.description: Enter the Zoho Connect Network ID (Scope ID). You can find it in any group under Settings > Developer Info.

setupGuide.title: How to connect Zoho Connect
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zoho account with a Zoho Connect network and access to the Zoho Developer Console to create or review your OAuth client.

steps.title: Open Zoho Connect and confirm your network is ready
steps.description: Sign in to Zoho Connect and finish creating the network you want to automate. Most Zoho Connect automations need a specific network context.

steps.title: Create or review your Zoho OAuth client
steps.description: Open the Zoho Developer Console, add a client ID if you do not already have one, and record the client ID and client secret for your Zoho Connect integration.

steps.title: Authorize the Zoho Connect scopes
steps.description: Start the OAuth authorization flow and approve the Zoho Connect scopes required by your selected actions. Request offline access so Zoho returns a refresh token, and use prompt=consent when you need the refresh token issued.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens
steps.description: Send the authorization code to Zoho's token endpoint to obtain an access token and refresh token.

steps.title: Find the network ID you want to automate
steps.description: Run the Get All Networks action or call the Get All Networks API to list the networks available to this connection, then copy the network ID you want to reuse for Connect actions that require scopeID.

setupGuide.title: Connect Zoho Creator
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zoho OAuth client in the same data center as your Zoho Creator account.

steps.title: Open the Zoho Developer Console
steps.description: Sign in and open the OAuth client you want MindCloud to use for Zoho Creator.

steps.title: Use a server-based client
steps.description: Create or edit a server-based client so Zoho can redirect the authorization code back to MindCloud after sign-in.

steps.title: Confirm the redirect URI
steps.description: Make sure the redirect URI registered in Zoho exactly matches the OAuth callback that MindCloud shows during connection setup.

steps.title: Authorize the full Zoho Creator scope set
steps.description: Authorize the connection with all documented Zoho Creator v2.1 scopes so the scaffolded app can cover records, metadata, files, dashboard, and bulk read actions.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Back in MindCloud, open the Zoho Creator connection, authenticate with Zoho, and approve access for the target Creator account.

setupGuide.title: Connect Zoho CRM
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to a Zoho API Console client for Zoho CRM.

steps.title: Open your Zoho API Console client
steps.description: Sign in to the Zoho API Console and open your Server-based application. If you do not have one yet, create a new Server-based application for Zoho CRM.

steps.title: Set the MindCloud redirect URI
steps.description: Add this redirect URI to the client: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/zohoCRM/callback

steps.title: Enter your Zoho client credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the Client ID and Client Secret from the Zoho API Console into the Zoho CRM connection form.

steps.title: Sign in with Zoho
steps.description: Click Authenticate in MindCloud. Zoho will redirect you to the correct accounts server during the OAuth flow and MindCloud will use the returned accounts-server value for token exchange.

steps.title: Choose your Zoho Accounts server
steps.description: Open Zoho's Multi-DC support page and copy the Accounts URL that matches your data center. Enter that full URL in MindCloud as Accounts Server.

steps.title: Start the OAuth connection in MindCloud
steps.description: Enter Accounts Server, then start the OAuth flow. MindCloud already uses the shared Zoho OAuth client configured for this app.

steps.title: Approve the Zoho consent screen
steps.description: Approve access for the Zoho Desk organization you want to connect. Zoho returns the token set and the Desk API location needed for later API calls.

steps.title: Use the token-bound organization by default
steps.description: Zoho Desk binds the OAuth token to a specific organization during consent and can infer org context from that token for later API calls. Only set Organization ID manually if you need an explicit override that matches the same bound portal.

setupGuide.title: Connect Zoho Inventory
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zoho Inventory account and a Zoho API Console server-based application that matches the shared OAuth client configured for this wrapper.

steps.title: Open the Zoho API Console application for this wrapper
steps.description: Open the server-based Zoho API Console application associated with this MindCloud wrapper and confirm the MindCloud redirect URL is allowed there.

steps.title: Enable the right data centers if needed
steps.description: If the Zoho Inventory users who will connect are outside your app's home data center, enable those data centers in the Zoho API Console. If your Zoho app uses separate credentials per data center, those credentials still must match the user who is authorizing.

steps.title: Start the connection in MindCloud
steps.description: Open the Zoho Inventory connection modal and click Connect. This wrapper now uses the shared OAuth client configured in the app, so you should not need to paste a client ID or secret during the normal auth flow.

steps.title: Choose the right Inventory organization
steps.description: After the connection succeeds, run List Organizations and pick an organization_id where org_joined_app_list includes inventory. Save that value into the optional Organization ID field for this connection before running the other actions.

name: Zoho Invoice
description: Create invoices, track expenses, and manage projects and payments

setupGuide.title: Connect Zoho Invoice
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zoho OAuth client in the same data center as your Zoho Invoice organization.

steps.title: Open the Zoho Developer Console
steps.description: Sign in and open the OAuth client you want MindCloud to use for Zoho Invoice.

steps.title: Confirm the redirect URI
steps.description: Make sure the redirect URI registered in Zoho exactly matches the OAuth callback that MindCloud shows during connection setup.

steps.title: Use the full Zoho Invoice scope
steps.description: Authorize the connection with ZohoInvoice.fullaccess.all so the scaffolded app has the full documented Stage 1 scope coverage.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Back in MindCloud, open the Zoho Invoice connection, authenticate with Zoho, and approve access for the target organization.

arguments.name: Tax Reg No
arguments.description: 12 digit Tax Registration number of a contact with Tax treatment as home_country_mexico , border_region_mexico , non_mexico . Consumers generic RFC: XAXX010101000 , Overseas generic RFC: XEXX010101000

arguments.name: Country Code
arguments.description: For UK Edition: Two letter country code of a contact For Avalara: Two letter country code for the customer country, if your customer is not in US. Refer [AvaTax Codes for Countries and States][2].

arguments.name: VAT Treatment
arguments.description: VAT treatment of the contact.Allowed Values: uk (A business that is located in the UK.), eu_vat_registered (A business that is reg for VAT and trade goods between Northern Ireland and EU. This node is available only for organizations enabled for NI protocal in VAT Settings.) and overseas (A business that is located outside UK. Pre Brexit, this was split as eu_vat_registered , eu_vat_not_registered and non_eu ).

setupGuide.title: Connect Zoho Mail
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to Zoho API Console and permission to create or edit a server-based OAuth client.

steps.title: Open Zoho API Console
steps.description: Open the Zoho API Console and create a Server-based Application, or open the existing OAuth client you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Register the exact MindCloud redirect URI
steps.description: In the OAuth client settings, add this redirect URI exactly, with the same case and no extra slash: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/zohoMail/callback . Zoho rejects the authorization request when the configured redirect URI does not exactly match the one sent by MindCloud.

steps.title: Copy the client credentials
steps.description: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the Zoho OAuth client.

steps.title: Finish the connection in MindCloud
steps.description: Back in MindCloud, enter the Client ID and Client Secret, continue the OAuth popup, and approve the requested Zoho Mail scopes ZohoMail.accounts.READ, ZohoMail.folders.ALL, ZohoMail.tags.ALL, and ZohoMail.messages.ALL.

name: Zoho Meeting
description: Zoho Meeting is Zoho's meetings and webinars platform. This wrapper covers Zoho Meeting's OAuth 2.0 API for managing organization context, license details, meetings, and webinars.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.notes: Zoho Meeting pricing currently lists API access on the Professional plan. After OAuth succeeds, run Get Current User Details to capture the zsoid/orgId used by most Meeting and Webinar actions.

credentials.name: Organization ID
credentials.description: Optional default Zoho Meeting organization ID (zsoid/orgId). Run Get Current User Details after connecting, then save the value you use most often.

credentials.name: Accounts Server URL
credentials.description: Zoho Accounts server URL for your data center. Use the default https://accounts.zoho.com unless your Zoho account authenticates against another regional Accounts host.

credentials.name: Meeting Host
credentials.description: Zoho Meeting host for your data center, such as meeting.zoho.com or meeting.zoho.eu. Check the browser URL after you sign in to Zoho Meeting if you are unsure.

setupGuide.title: Connect Zoho Meeting
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zoho API Console server-based application for Zoho Meeting, and Zoho Meeting pricing currently lists API access on the Professional plan.

steps.title: Open or create your Zoho OAuth app
steps.description: Open the Zoho API Console and use a server-based application for Zoho Meeting. If you do not have one yet, register a new app there so you can copy a Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Add the MindCloud redirect URL
steps.description: In your Zoho app settings, add the MindCloud redirect URL shown in this connection to the allowed redirect URIs.

steps.title: Confirm your plan includes API access
steps.description: Zoho Meeting pricing currently lists API access under the Professional plan. Confirm the account you plan to connect has that entitlement before you continue.

steps.title: Enter your client credentials and connect
steps.description: Paste the Client ID and Client Secret into this connection, keep the scope set provided by the app, then click Connect and complete the Zoho consent screen.

steps.title: Capture your organization ID
steps.description: After the connection succeeds, run Get Current User Details and copy the zsoid value from the response. Save it in the optional Organization ID field if you want most meeting and webinar actions to default to the same organization.

name: Zoho Recruit
description: Manage candidates, job records, users, and recruiting data

setupGuide.title: Connect Zoho Recruit
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zoho Recruit OAuth client. If you already have a Client ID and Client Secret, you can reuse them.

steps.title: Open the Zoho API Console
steps.description: Go to the Zoho API Console and create or open a Server-based application for Zoho Recruit.

steps.title: Confirm the redirect URI
steps.description: In your Zoho client, add the Redirect URI shown in the MindCloud connection dialog exactly as it appears.

steps.title: Enter your client details in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the Client ID and Client Secret into the MindCloud connection form. Keep Accounts Server URL as the default unless your Recruit account uses another Zoho Accounts region.

steps.title: Connect and approve access
steps.description: Click Connect and approve the requested Zoho Recruit scopes in the browser popup.

setupGuide.title: Set up Zoho Sign OAuth
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zoho account with access to Zoho Sign. If you already have a Client ID and Client Secret, you can skip the client-creation step.

steps.title: Open Zoho Developer Console
steps.description: Sign in with the Zoho account that manages your Zoho Sign organization.

steps.title: Create or review a server-based client
steps.description: Choose Server-based Applications. Enter a client name, your homepage URL, and the exact redirect URI that MindCloud shows during connection setup, then create the client.

steps.title: Copy the client credentials into MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the Client ID and Client Secret into this app configuration so MindCloud can start the Zoho OAuth flow.

steps.title: Confirm your Zoho domain suffix
steps.description: Open your Zoho Sign web app and note the domain suffix in the URL. Supported Zoho Sign data center suffixes are com, eu, in, jp, com.au, zohocloud.ca, and sa. Enter that value in the Zoho Domain field.

steps.title: Enable Multi DC when one client must work across Zoho regions
steps.description: Zoho documents that OAuth clients are data-center specific by default. If this client will be reused across multiple Zoho data centers, enable Multi DC in Zoho Developer Console.

setupGuide.title: Connect Zoho Sprints
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Use a Zoho account that can access the Zoho Sprints workspace you want MindCloud to use, and confirm that API access is enabled in that workspace first.

steps.title: Enable API access in the Zoho Sprints workspace
steps.description: In the target Zoho Sprints workspace settings, enable API access before you try to connect the app in MindCloud.

steps.title: Start the connection in MindCloud
steps.description: Open the Zoho Sprints connection flow in MindCloud and continue to the Zoho authorization page.

setupGuide.title: How to set up your Zoho Writer connection
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Sign in to a Zoho account that can open Zoho Writer in the browser. If you plan to use combine or store actions, make sure the same account also has Zoho WorkDrive access. If you plan to use sign actions, make sure the account has Zoho Sign credits available.

steps.title: Open Zoho Writer once
steps.description: Go to Zoho Writer and confirm the account you want to connect can open the Writer dashboard in the browser.

steps.title: Open each merge template once before using merge actions
steps.description: For merge, combine, email, store, invoke, or sign flows, open the template in Zoho Writer and access its Automate area at least once before the first API run. Zoho's API docs call this out as a prerequisite for these flows.

steps.title: Connect your Zoho account in MindCloud
steps.description: Start the connection from MindCloud, sign in to Zoho, and approve the requested Writer, WorkDrive, and Zoho Sign scopes for the actions you plan to use.

setupGuide.title: Set up Zoho OAuth for ZeptoMail
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Zoho API Console and the ZeptoMail account that owns the management resources.

steps.title: Create a Zoho server-based OAuth client
steps.description: Create a new Server-based Application in the Zoho API Console for ZeptoMail management access.

steps.title: Register the MindCloud callback URL
steps.description: Add this redirect URI to the Zoho OAuth client: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/zohoZeptoMail/callback

steps.title: Grant the ZeptoMail scopes
steps.description: Authorize the client with these exact scopes: Zeptomail.email.All, Zeptomail.Suppressions.All, Zeptomail.MailTemplates.All, Zeptomail.Domains.All, Zeptomail.Exports.All.

steps.title: Enter the OAuth client values in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the Client ID and Client Secret into the MindCloud connection form, then start the OAuth connect flow.

steps.title: Complete the Zoho consent flow
steps.description: Sign in to the correct Zoho account and approve the requested scopes.

authentication.name: Send Mail Token

setupGuide.title: Set up a ZeptoMail send-mail connection
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the ZeptoMail account and the Mail Agent that will send emails.

steps.title: Open the Mail Agent you want to use
steps.description: Each ZeptoMail Mail Agent has its own Send Mail Token and alias.

steps.title: Copy or generate the Send Mail Token
steps.description: In the Email API area for that Mail Agent, generate the Send Mail Token if needed and copy the full value.

steps.title: Copy the Agent Alias
steps.description: Copy the Mail Agent alias from the same agent details page.

steps.title: Enter the values in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the Send Mail Token into the API Key field and paste the Agent Alias into the Agent Alias field.

PKCE is disabled for this wrapper because the current Zoom app/authorize flow is rejecting the code_challenge_method during connection setup. Zoom must have the exact MindCloud redirect URI allowlisted: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/zoomTeamChat/callback . Redirect URI matching is exact, including case.

setupGuide.title: Set up your Zoom OAuth app
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: This Zoom Team Chat connector uses the dedicated MindCloud callback for the Team Chat app.

steps.title: Configure the Zoom redirect URI
steps.description: In the Zoom OAuth app, set both the Redirect URL for OAuth and the OAuth allow list to https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/zoomTeamChat/callback exactly.

steps.title: Keep Team Chat scopes enabled in Zoom
steps.description: Enable the Team Chat scopes needed by this wrapper directly on the Zoom app.

steps.title: Retry Connect in MindCloud
steps.description: Retry the OAuth popup for the current draft test connection after saving the Zoom app settings.

name: Zubie
description: Access Zubie Zinc fleet telematics data including accounts, devices, events, groups, places, schedules, tags, trips, users, vehicles, media, and visits.

authentication.name: OAuth2
authentication.description: Connect a Zubie Zinc account using OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow.
authentication.notes: Create your Zinc app in the Zubie developer portal, set the redirect URI to https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/zubie/callback, then use Connect to authorize a Zubie account. Additional scopes require Zubie approval.

setupGuide.title: Connect your Zubie account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zubie Zinc developer app with the redirect URI set to https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/zubie/callback.

steps.title: Open the Zubie developer app settings
steps.description: Sign in to the Zubie Zinc developer portal and open the app you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Verify your redirect URI
steps.description: Make sure the app redirect URI is exactly https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/zubie/callback.

steps.title: Verify the allowed scopes
steps.description: Confirm the app includes the read scopes account.read, account_activity.read, places.read, user.read, and vehicles.read. If you need broader access, request approval from Zubie before connecting.

steps.title: Connect in MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and start the OAuth connection. MindCloud will open Zubie’s consent flow so you can sign in and approve access for the Zubie account you want to use.

description: Zulip: Send messages and manage channels, users, and events

authentication.name: Basic
authentication.description: Authenticate with a Zulip bot email, API key, and realm URL.

credentials.name: Site URL
credentials.description: Your Zulip server URL, for example https://your-org.zulipchat.com

setupGuide.title: Connect Zulip
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Zulip bot account in the organization you want to connect.

steps.title: Sign in to Zulip
steps.description: Open your Zulip web or desktop app and sign in to the correct organization. If your organization uses Google sign in, you can use that to access the UI.

steps.title: Open bot settings
steps.description: Click the gear icon in the upper right corner, select Personal settings, and then click Bots in the left sidebar.

steps.title: Copy the bot API key
steps.description: In the Actions column, click the manage bot icon for the bot you want to connect. Scroll to API key and copy the API key.

steps.title: Copy the bot email and site URL
steps.description: Use the bot's email address as the Username field in MindCloud. Use your Zulip organization URL, such as https://your-org.zulipchat.com, as the Site URL field.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud connection
steps.description: In MindCloud, enter Username = bot email, Password = API key, and Site URL = your Zulip organization URL, then run Test Connection.

name: Zyllio
description: Zyllio Public API access for workspace metadata, table rows, file uploads, and push notifications.

authentication.name: API key
authentication.description: Connect to the Zyllio Public API with a workspace API key sent in the x-api-key header.

setupGuide.title: Set up your Zyllio API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the target Zyllio workspace before you connect this app.

steps.title: Open the workspace dashboard
steps.description: Sign in to Zyllio and open the workspace you want this connection to access.

steps.title: Copy the workspace API key
steps.description: Open the Zyllio API or SaaS integration settings for that workspace and copy the API key that authorizes the Public API.

steps.title: Confirm the API base URL
steps.description: Zyllio publishes its OpenAPI docs at https://www.zyllio.one/api/docs/ and serves the public API under https://www.zyllio.one/api/public.

name: Zyte
description: Access Zyte Stats API reports through curated analytics actions over the official stats endpoint.

authentication.name: Dashboard API Key (Basic Auth)
authentication.description: Authenticate to Zyte Stats with your dashboard API key as the Basic-auth username and an empty password.
authentication.notes: Zyte documents Basic authentication with the dashboard API key as the username. Runtime verification shows the password value is ignored by the Stats API, so MindCloud can use any placeholder password to satisfy its required-field contract.

credentials.name: Organization ID
credentials.description: Your Zyte organization ID, available in the Zyte dashboard and required by the Stats API.

setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Use your Zyte dashboard API key as the Username field. Zyte Stats authenticates with HTTP Basic and requires your organization ID on every request.

steps.title: Open the Zyte dashboard
steps.description: Sign in to app.zyte.com with an account that can view API keys and organization settings.

steps.title: Copy your dashboard API key
steps.description: Open the area where Zyte exposes dashboard API keys and copy the key you want to use for Stats API access.

steps.title: Copy your organization ID
steps.description: Find the Zyte organization identifier for the account whose Stats API usage you want to query.

steps.title: Fill the MindCloud connection form
steps.description: Paste the dashboard API key into Username, enter any short placeholder into Password, and paste your Zyte organization ID into Organization ID.

arguments.name: End Time
arguments.description: Optional end of the reporting window in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to the current time when omitted by Zyte.

arguments.name: Start Time
arguments.description: Optional start of the reporting window in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to seven days ago when omitted by Zyte.
